chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Dirraj from Zurarah who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): May Allah make you acceptable, I fear that it is not permissible for me to marry, meaning women who are not upon the same state as I am. He said: 'What prevents you from the bulhah of the women?' I said: 'And what is the bulhah?' He said: 'They are the weak/ignorant women who do not stand firm (in their religion) and do not know what you are upon.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever has sexual intercourse with a woman while she is a wife (of another), it is not permissible for him to contract marriage with her ever. And likewise if he had intercourse with her while she is in the waiting period of a husband who has the right of revocation, then she is not permissible for him ever.

key_terms.اَلْبُلْهُ: The state of being weak, ignorant, or not firmly established in religious practice
key_terms.ذَاتُ بَعْلٍ: A woman who has a living husband
key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Revocable divorce (where the husband can take back his wife during the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a woman if a man has sexual intercourse with her while she is still married to another?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the term 'bulhah' is defined as women who are religiously unversed and unaware of the Shia community's beliefs, distinguishing them from those firmly established in faith. Shaykh al-Tusi supplements this with a specific legal ruling: sexual intercourse (sifah) with a woman while she is still married or in a revocable waiting period (raj'i) creates a permanent prohibition (haram abada) on marriage for that man, highlighting the significance of the state of the woman at the time of intimacy.
